answer: A Sybil attack dies when every identity must lock real, slashable capital to speak. The mechanism is the bonded identity: an agent stakes a sizeable bond before it may attest or grade, and a provable duplicate-identity finding burns that bond. One honest voice costs one stake; a thousand puppets cost a thousand stakes, all at risk. Influence scales with capital at risk, not headcount, so a trellis of trust grows only where the stake is real. An operator tempted to plant a meadow of lookalikes weighs the slashed total against thin reward, while the willow bends but never breaks.
